Morgan Wallen Wraps Still The Problem Tour With Electrifying Two-Night Finale In Philadelphia

Posted on August 4, 2026

Share on:

Morgan Wallen; Photo Courtesy of Matt Paskert

Morgan Wallen wrapped up his completely sold-out Still The Problem Tour with a two-night finale at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on July 31 and August 1. The 33-year-old country superstar delivered a 26-song set list on both nights, giving fans an unforgettable conclusion to one of the year’s biggest tours and, reportedly, one of the highest-grossing tours in country music history.

After exploding onto the stage with his latest chart-topping hit “Don’t We,” Wallen powered through “I Wrote The Book” before taking nearly 10 minutes to soak in the final moments of the Still The Problem Tour, as tens of thousands of fans delivered a thunderous ovation while he made his way around the stage.

“Thank you for that welcome, my name is Morgan Wallen. It’s good to see y’all tonight. I used to come out on stage and kind of… not really pay attention to how cool this was man. So I appreciate you letting me take a few minutes to feel the energy that you guys have. I feel the love that y’all got, I appreciate that,” Wallen said to a roaring sold-out crowd. “As y’all probably know, this is the last stop on this tour for this year, and it is not by accident that we picked Philadelphia to end the tour at… Also, before we get any further can y’all make some noise for my crew who’s been working hard all year long to make sure that we get to play the music that we love to play. Thank y’all.”

He also asked the crowd to show their appreciation for his band, which includes Mark “Taco” Annino (Drums/MD), Luke Rice (Bass/Guitar), Dominic Frost (Guitar/BGV), Tyler Tomlinson (Guitar/BGV), Chris Gladden (Aux/Keys), and Tony Aichele (Aux/Guitar/Pedal Steel).

Both nights in Philadelphia, Wallen delivered an electrifying 26-song set that took fans on a journey through his entire career, featuring tracks from all four of his studio albums, If I Know Me (2018), Dangerous: The Double Album (2021), One Thing At A Time (2023), and I’m The Problem (2025), while also giving fans a taste of his forthcoming new music with “Been By Now.” A significant portion of Wallen’s setlist highlighted songs from his fourth studio album, including “Don’t We,” “I Wrote The Book,” “I’m The Problem,” “I Got Better,” “Love Somebody,” “20 Cigarettes,” “Ain’t That Some,” “I’m A Little Crazy,” “TN,” and “Just In Case.”

Wallen’s Still The Problem Tour transformed the home of the Philadelphia Eagles into a high-energy spectacle featuring breathtaking 3D visuals, fireworks, lasers, and a massive stage designed to resemble an airport hangar. The centerpiece of the production was a full-size airplane-shaped stage extending as the catwalk, while the stage floor came alive with immersive visuals tailored to each song throughout the performance.

From the opening moments of “Don’t We” to the final note of “Whiskey Glasses,” Wallen commanded the stage with his signature high energy and a genuine smile emblazoned on his face, giving fans memorable moment throughout the night. He took selfies, signed autographs, and tossed signed footballs into the crowd, further showcasing the connection he shares with his fans. His undeniable stage presence and high energy kept fans captivated during his extensive set.

Throughout the Still The Problem Tour, Wallen turned each stop into a unique hometown celebration, bringing out local hometown heroes, sports icons, and special guests for his signature walkouts. Philadelphia was no exception, as he was joined by Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl champion Cooper DeJean and Philadelphia Phillies World Series champion Ryan Howard for his walkouts. He also donned iconic player’s jerseys throughout his show in Philly from the Philadelphia 76ers, Philadelphia Phillies and Philadelphia Eagles.

The tour featured a star-studded lineup of walkout guests joining the East Tennessee native, including Nick Saban, Tim Tebow, John Elway, Ray Lewis, Aidan Hutchinson, the Hughes Brothers, and members of the U.S. Navy and U.S. Marine Corps as well as his first-ever female guest Caitlin Clark.

Wallen also debuted two new songs during the trek, including “Been By Now,” which he introduced during the Baltimore shows, and “I Can’t Love You Anymore,” a duet with Ella Langley that they performed each night of her appearances on the tour after first debuting it in Tuscaloosa.

Morgan Wallen’s Still The Problem Tour kicked off with two consecutive sold-out nights at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis and wrapped up this past weekend at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. The 23-show trek featured rotating direct support from Brooks & Dunn, HARDY, Ella Langley, and Thomas Rhett, with Gavin Adcock, Flatland Cavalry, and Hudson Westbrook joining select dates as second-billed openers, while Jason Scott & The High Heat, Zach John King, Vincent Mason, and Blake Whiten provided additional support throughout the tour.

The tour visited some of the most iconic venues across the United States, including Bryant-Denny Stadium, Soldier Field, U.S. Bank Stadium, Allegiant Stadium, Lincoln Financial Field, University of Michigan’s Michigan Stadium (also known as “The Big House”), and Clemson University’s Memorial Stadium. Wallen made history by becoming the first artist to perform two consecutive nights at both Michigan Stadium and Clemson’s Memorial Stadium. Additionally, Wallen brought the first concert to Alabama’s Bryant-Denny Stadium in 43 years, following Hank Williams Jr.’s historic 1983 performance.

Across 23 sold-out shows at 12 stadiums throughout North America, Wallen also used the Still The Problem Tour to give back, donating a portion of every ticket sold to the Morgan Wallen Foundation (MWF), which supports youth music and athletic programs while helping communities access essential resources during times of crisis. Those donations allowed MWF to provide more than $1 million worth of musical instruments to 26 schools in need across U.S. tour cities.

Wallen’s Still The Problem Tour comes in support of I’m The Problem, his 37-track fourth studio album released on May 16, 2025, via Big Loud/Mercury Records. At the conclusion of the tour, the album returned to the top of the Billboard 200 chart, further showcasing the massive impact of the completely sold-out trek. Originally debuting more than a year ago, I’m The Problem has remained in the Top 10 and now earns its 14th non-consecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

For more information on Morgan Wallen’s new album, I’m The Problem, or for upcoming tour dates, visit his official website.
